payload.title: Triton Embraces Tile IR: Beyond SIMT
payload.summary: An analysis of the Triton-to-tile-IR experimental project, which introduces CUDA Tile IR as a native tile-based intermediate representation for Triton compilation on Blackwell GPUs.

sections.heading: 1. Why Triton-to-tile-IR?
sections.gist: Historically, Triton relied on generating PTX (NVIDIA's virtual ISA) to drive GPUs.

sections.heading: 2. Four Core Capabilities of the Tile IR Backend
sections.gist: While Triton already supports new architecture features, efficiency is limited.

sections.heading: 3. Current Status
sections.gist: The project is in early incubation, **supporting only CUDA 13.1 and Blackwell architecture**.

sections.heading: 4. Getting Started
sections.gist: With a Blackwell GPU available, enable the new compilation path with:

sections.heading: 5. Conclusion
sections.gist: From Thread to Tile — the change is not merely lexical but represents a fundamental shift in how compilers understand hardware.

implementation.snippet:
```bash
# Install the project
pip install -e .

# Enable the Tile IR compiler switch
export ENABLE_TILE=1

# Run your Triton kernel
python your_triton_script.py
```
